methods: SHA-256, byte size and page count checked before catalog comparison.

All 61 pages of the six accessible PDFs were extracted in order and all 61 were rendered. The six sparse/attachment pages in EM_Hauling_Info_2018.pdf were visually checked, including both photos, attachment cover sheets, rotated chain-of-custody page and sample receiving/log-in page.
The prior complete batch-99 carrier review was retained for EPA_PCB_2014.pdf, Oscoda_2022.pdf and their three derivative images; no derivative was treated as a new record.
Existing canonical records were reused; no source file was overwritten and no duplicate catalog record was created.

contentFindings.finding: The Cadillac NPDES SIU information sheet identifies Wexford County Landfill LLC, permit 590-13, at 990 U.S. 131 N., and reports process wastewater averaging 33,000 gallons per day with intermittent discharge.
contentFindings.boundary: Aggregate SIU-profile estimate only; no load date/time, actual load gallons, hauler, receiving entry, invoice, agreement or cessation date.

contentFindings.pages: PDF pages 1-6 and 49-50; embedded Pace report pages 1-44
contentFindings.finding: The May 8, 2018 email concerns photos from an application site and a Pace biosolids analysis, naming fields 20N7W7-RJ01, 21N9W19TC01, 21N9W20TC01 and 21N9W30GR01. Pace project 4610111 covers Holding Tank 4 solid and water samples collected 03/28/18 13:40 and received 03/29/18 12:40. The reviewed photos show a Midwest Injection Inc. tanker and GEA Houle land-application equipment. The receiving checklist records 1.9, 2.7 and 2.1 C and notes biosolids were more aqueous than solids.
contentFindings.boundary: Outbound biosolids land application and laboratory custody, not inbound Wexford-leachate delivery; no Wexford manifest, Cadillac receiving log, invoice or final-load date.

contentFindings.finding: The July 30, 2018 IPP PFAS interim report lists Wexford County Landfill LLC at 990 N. US Hwy 131 as a probable source, says it was in the DEQ WMRPD initiative, and says POTW effluent monitoring was deferred while industrial-user results were pending.
contentFindings.boundary: Screening/progress submission, not a laboratory result or delivery record; listed attachments were not part of this batch.

contentFindings.finding: The November 29, 2018 IPP PFAS summary says Wexford landfill sampling was completed by the POTW and received, identifies J17646-1 as the leachate report, records Cadillac's contact with the landfill, and states that the landfill refused to invest in cleanup. It reports no PFAS biosolids monitoring in that submission.
contentFindings.boundary: Submitted summary and reported statement only; not an independent load-by-load history or final-delivery date.

contentFindings.finding: The June 28, 2019 status report links J17646-1, identifies Wexford as the confirmed source, says Wexford had gone to deep-well injection and would not bring leachate anymore, and records a June 4, 2019 effluent result at 2 MGD with PFOS 7.1 ng/L and PFOA 15 ng/L. The status is 'PFOS eliminated'; Jeffrey Dietlin's draft/submitted times are 3:19:42 PM and 3:46:11 PM, with signed copy-of-record at 3:46:12 PM.
contentFindings.boundary: Source and cessation context plus one effluent result; no final-load date, time, gallons, driver, truck, manifest or invoice.

contentFindings.finding: The 2020 IPP annual-report summary addresses approved-method influent, effluent and biosolids analyses, pass-through, permit-limit problems and biosolids disposal.
contentFindings.boundary: Summary form only; no Wexford receiving entry, leachate load, invoice or source-specific PFAS result.

contentFindings.pages: Prior full review: PDF page 199 / printed page 198
contentFindings.finding: EPA's 2014 PCB handler report lists Northern A-1 Services, EPA ID MID020906814, as a transporter and names American Waste as the owner facility.
contentFindings.boundary: Registry entry, not a shipment record; no PFAS handling or proof of Wexford-to-Cadillac leachate transport.

contentFindings.pages: Prior full review: PDF pages 5, 61 and 397-416
contentFindings.finding: The Oscoda report and bill of lading 05032-22 document a separate 2022 movement of three drums of investigation-derived PFAS soil, quantity 1,500 UOM P, with Northern A-1, truck 817 and trailer 193. Later pages are QC, receipt and isotope-dilution support.
contentFindings.boundary: Outside 2009-July 2019 and neither landfill leachate nor a Cadillac WWTP receipt; disposal-facility field names Northern A-1 Services.

queueDecision: No receiving-history requirement is closed. This batch strengthens the distinction between outbound biosolids land application, IPP/PFAS reporting and the unresolved Wexford-to-Cadillac load history. Carrier/PCB/Oscoda materials remain later context, not proof of Cadillac leachate deliveries.
